title: Lyon 2021 split-arc mesh extractor (replaces QEx as actual final-output path)
description:
Critical finding from PATCH-62 investigation. metriko's reference hand-quad.obj is NOT produced by their QEx (qex/) — it's produced by their visualizer/tmesh/ split-arc extractor. QEx is shipped as an alternative but unused for final output. This is THE Lyon 2021 approach: take quantized T-mesh, split each T-edge into q_i sub-arcs, assemble quads from those splits.

Source files in metriko (~784 LOC):
- gen_qgp_vert.h    (79 LOC) — split T-edge vertices
- gen_qgp_edge.h    (143 LOC) — split arcs
- gen_qgp_table.h   (69 LOC) — per-Tquad split table
- gen_qgp_mesh.h    (91 LOC) — mesh assembly
- visualize_qgp_vert.h, visualize_qgp_edge.h, visualize_qgp_mesh.h, visualize_tedge.h — orchestrators

Inputs: T-mesh + quantization vector X + per-corner UVs + matching.
Output: quad mesh (V_quad, F_quad).

This is the algorithm that closes the loop on Lyon 2021 reproducibility. PATCH-43/58/61/62 (QEx) is a parallel/lateral approach worth keeping but not on the critical path.
definition-of-done: New package quadlayout/lyon2021/ implements the split-arc mesh extractor. MetrikoStageRegressionTest gains a stage 2+3+4 -> mesh extractor test that compares quad count vs hand-quad.obj's 2339. Existing 78 quadlayout tests still pass.
testing-plan: 1. Port gen_qgp_vert/edge/table/mesh.h to Java. 2. Run on metriko's stage2/3/4 inputs, compare quad count + topology to hand-quad.obj. 3. Match within 5% on Hand-30k.
